facility_roles.note: Start: year of settling. End: latest evidence (2011), see the experiment intervals. The experiment ran in the Canfranc laboratory at 2450 m.w.e. (called the old laboratory in the 2011 talk); the Atlas holds one approximate point for the laboratory.
facility_roles.quote: The ROSEBUD experiment for Direct Dark Matter detection settled in 1999 in the Canfranc Underground Laboratory.

intervals.label: WIMP search with cryogenic bolometers at the (old) Canfranc laboratory
intervals.note: Start: 'settled in 1999' (year). The first phase used sapphire and germanium absorbers; the second phase CaWO4, BGO, LiF and sapphire scintillating bolometers. End: bounded by the latest source read, a November 2011 talk reporting the move to the new LSC halls.
intervals.quote: The ROSEBUD experiment for Direct Dark Matter detection settled in 1999 in the Canfranc Underground Laboratory.

intervals.label: completed (no end date published)
intervals.note: The 2011 talk says ROSEBUD was moving to Hall B of the new LSC and planned to restart measurements in 2012; no source read reports measurements after 2011 or a formal end, so this is the year of the latest evidence, not a published end date.
intervals.quote: ROSEBUD is currently moving to the Hall B in the new LSC facilities planning to restart measurements in 2012.

quantity.note: Three sapphire (Al2O3) bolometers of the first runs.
quantity.quote: It consists of three small sapphire bolometers (of a total mass of 100 g) with NTD-Ge sensors in a dilution refrigerator operating at 20 mK in the Canfranc Underground Laboratory

quantity.note: Threshold lower than 450 eV on the germanium bolometer; lower than 1 keV on the sapphire ones.
quantity.quote: Thresholds respectively lower than 1keV and 450 eV were achieved on these detectors.

name: ROSEBUD
notes: external.inspire_experiment is null: INSPIRE was not consulted (its rate budget belongs to the supervised importer).
A 90% C.L. spin-independent exclusion plot derived from the sapphire runs appears in the body of arXiv:astro-ph/0004292; the abstract states no limit, so the result is recorded as a measurement.
The 2011 talk's slide 'ROSEBUD 1995 - 2011' (beside a picture of the old Canfranc laboratory) is ambiguous about what the years delimit and is not used for a date.

ROSEBUD joined the proposed EURECA project (a one-tonne cryogenic array proposed for an extension of the Modane laboratory); EURECA is not recorded because no design report and no approval were found.
Latest evidence is a November 2011 talk (restart in the new LSC planned for 2012); the end is recorded as 'completed' with low confidence and no end date.
Placement: the Canfranc laboratory (2450 m.w.e.); the Atlas has one approximate point for the LSC.

physics_goals.quote: an experiment which attempts to detect low mass Weak Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs) through their elastic scattering off Al and O nuclei
physics_goals.value: Detect low-mass WIMPs through their elastic scattering off Al and O nuclei with cryogenic sapphire bolometers

summary.plain: ROSEBUD was a set of tiny crystals cooled to a few hundredths of a degree above absolute zero, in the Canfranc underground laboratory in the Spanish Pyrenees, built to catch the faint heat from dark matter particles hitting aluminium, oxygen or germanium nuclei. It mainly tested detector materials and cut backgrounds.
summary.technical: Cryogenic bolometers (sapphire Al2O3 25-50 g, Ge 67 g, then scintillating CaWO4 54 g, BGO 46 g, LiF) with NTD-Ge thermistors in a mobile dilution refrigerator at 20 mK, in the Canfranc laboratory (2450 m.w.e.); thresholds below 1 keV (sapphire) and 450 eV (Ge); phase two added light read-out for nuclear-recoil discrimination. A move to Hall B of the new LSC was planned for 2012.
